newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FOCUS - Job cut spectre revisits S.Africa gold mines.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Job cut spectre revisits S.Africa gold mines.

text.p: The spectre of job cuts loomed anew over the South African mining industry on Thursday with the world's biggest gold producer threatening shaft closures in the face of a sickly bullion price.
Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd said losses at shafts within its Free State Consolidated Gold Mines Ltd company (Freegold) were unsustainable and the shafts might close.

"Four shafts at Freegold incurred losses which totalled 18 million rand. On current performance these shafts place an unsustainable burden on Freegold and will have to close," said Bobby Godsell, chief executive of Anglo's gold mines.
But the axe does not hang over Freegold alone.
Anglo's Vaal Reefs Exploration and Mining Co also warned of major job cuts with some shafts continuing to fall short of production targets and incurring losses.
"We will have to investigate compulsory retrenchments...we will have to make fairly significant reductions," Vaal Reefs mine manager Dick Fisher said.
Announcing gold results for the March quarter, Anglo showed a 34 percent slump in available profit to 224.3 million rand.
While much could be blamed on a four percent decrease in gold price received in the quarter -- due to bullion's slide and a stronger rand -- fewer productive shifts had been worked.
Godsell said there was a critical need for South African gold mines to work all the productive shifts possible to counter the decline in gold output due to ageing mines and falling grades.

"The goal must be for mines to operate every day they can profitably. The South African gold industry simply has to make meaningful progress towards this goal this year. In the current gold price scenario we need more rapid progress," he added.
Freegold -- the world's biggest gold mine -- last year faced the closure of five shafts and the sacking of 10,000 miners, triggering angry reaction from unions and government.
That crisis was resolved after negotiations secured an increase in shifts worked, but Freegold's future once again looks gloomy.

"Freegold has had a most disappointing quarter. Given its margins it's more vulnerable to the lower (gold) price. Its production was half a tonne of gold lower than last quarter and significantly below management's expectations," Godsell said.

Available profit at Freegold slumped 43 percent to 62.9 million rand in the first quarter. Of particular concern was the performance of Steyn Nos 2 and 5 and Freddies No 5 and the combined Western Holdings 2/3 shaft in the marginal category.
"As before management will work with labour to explore every avenue to avoid or delay such closures," Godsell said.

Vaal Reefs' Fisher said that the future of the mine's No 3 shaft remained in balance and decisive steps would have to be taken soon. "We anticipate having to withdraw our labour from the No 3 shaft," he said. Vaal Reefs posted available profit for the quarter of 77.3 million rand versus 101.7 million rand.

Godsell said that, with the exception of East Rand Gold and Uranium Co Ltd, Anglo's mining companies reported between six or seven fewer production shifts in the March quarter compared to the December quarter.
Furthermore, he warned that next week's two public holidays -- on Monday and Thursday -- would hit production.
Anglo is not alone in posting poor March quarter results. Gold Fields of South Africa Ltd, JCI Ltd and Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd have all announced sharp declines in profit.
Gengold Ltd is the only one of the major mining houses that have reported so far to buck the trend, helped by a tax rebate and the cancellation of consulting fees.
